 \qquad \kappa_c>0,
\]

proposed.statement: For \(K=2\) and \(c=(1,-1)\), the published reduced scalar minimax problem has a unique minimizer \(f_n^\star\), which is the posterior mean of \((p_+-p_-)/n\) given \(X_2\) under a least-favorable prior \(\pi_n^\star\) on \((p_+,p_-,r_0)\), and the scalar minimax value is the Bayes risk of \(\pi_n^\star\). A separate published reduction theorem proves that the unrestricted full binary two-arm game has the same minimax value and that balanced Bernoulli assignment with \(f_n^\star(\sum_i S_i)\) is minimax and admissible. The published Airy results give an explicit scalar nonlinear-shrinkage upper sequence and a scalar prior sequence whose Bayes risks attain the matching \(n^{-4/3}\) lower expansion. The cited source does not itself construct \(\pi_n^\star\) as a prior on complete response schedules and does not assert that this scalar prior, without a separate lift, is a Bayes-risk converse against arbitrary full-data procedures.

source.verbatim_statement: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:simplified_model_minimax_risk}\begin{equation}\label{eq:simplified_minimax_risk} r_n^* = \rho_n^* = \inf_f \sup_{\cl{I}_n} \E\left(f(p + \textsf{Bin}(r,1/2)) - \frac{p-q}{n} \right)^2.\end{equation} Moreover, there is a unique $f^*_n$ minimizing \eqref{eq:simplified_minimax_risk} and it is the posterior mean of $(p-q)/n$ under a least-favorable prior $\pi_n^*$ on $\cl{I}_n$. As a consequence, $f^*_n$ is admissible and $\rho_n^*$ is the Bayes risk of $\pi_n^*.$ \end{theorem} \begin{theorem}\label{thm:minimax_risk_reduction} Let $f_n^*$ be the function minimizing \eqref{eq:simplified_minimax_risk} in the reduced model. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:minimax_risk_is_equal_to_simplified_minimax_risk}\inf_{\cl{A}, \hat \tau} \sup_{\cl{P} \in \set{0,1}^{2n}} R_n(\cl{A},\hat \tau) = \rho_n^*.\end{equation} A minimax procedure achieving the upper bound is given by Bernoulli$(1/2)$ randomization with corresponding estimator $\hat{\tau}_{\Opt}=f^*_n(\sum_{i=1}^n S_i)$. Furthermore, this procedure is admissible. \end{theorem} \begin{theorem}\label{thm:second_order_minimax_risk_behavior_detailed_upper_bound} The estimator $\hat \tau_n^A(X) := \frac{X}{n} - \frac{1}{n^{2/3}}h_A\left( \frac{X}{n^{2/3}}\right)$ satisfies the risk bound \[\sup_{(\theta,r) \in \Theta_n} \E[(\hat \tau_n^A(X) - \theta/n)^2] \leq \frac{1}{n} - \frac{C_A}{n^{4/3}} + o_n(n^{-4/3}).\] \end{theorem} \begin{theorem}\label{thm:second_order_minimax_risk_behavior_detailed_lower_bound} The priors $\Pi_n$ on $\Theta_n$ defined by \begin{align*}& \Pi_n((0,n)) \propto \phi_A(0)^2 \\ & \Pi_n((k,n-k)) = \Pi_n((-k,n-k)) \propto \frac{1}{2}\phi_A\left(\frac{k}{n^{2/3}}\right)^2, \quad 1\leq k \leq n.\end{align*} have Bayes risks lower bounded by $\frac{1}{n} - \frac{C_A}{n^{4/3}} + o_n(n^{-4/3}).$ \end{theorem}

A rigorous partial answer is available.  Fix \(K\geq2\) and a nonzero zero-sum contrast \(c\).

First, if \(|S_c|=2\), then contrast-weighted independent assignment, with probability \(1/2\) on each active arm, and the coefficient-rescaled published two-arm posterior-mean rule form an exact finite-\(n\) minimax saddle.  The correspondingly embedded published least-favorable prior is an exact Bayes-risk converse.  In particular, if \(\rho_{n,2}=\rho_n((1,-1))\), then
\[
 \rho_n(c)=C_0(c)\rho_{n,2},
 \qquad
 d_n(c)=C_0(c)C_A n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]

Second, for arbitrary support, the independent \(q^\star\) design and the explicit clipped-shrinkage estimator in the universal second-order rate theorem satisfy, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \max_z R_n(\mathcal D^\star,\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sh}};z)
 \leq C_0(c)\{n^{-1}-\kappa_c n^{-4/3}\},
 \qquad \kappa_c>0,
\]
where \(\kappa_c\) is the explicit constant in that theorem.  Together with the embedded two-arm converse, this gives
\[
 0<C_0(c)\kappa_c
 \leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)
 \leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)
 \leq C_0(c)C_A.
\]

Third, choose rational nonzero zero-sum contrasts \(c^{(n)}\in\mathbb Q^K\) with \(c^{(n)}\to c\), put
\[
 \eta_n=\frac{L_{c-c^{(n)}}}{2},
\]
and choose integers \(M_n\geq1\).  Let
\[
 B_n=B_{n,c^{(n)}}(\nu_{n,M_n,c^{(n)}}),
 \qquad
 U_n=U_{n,M_n}(c^{(n)})
\]
be the exact rational prior and procedure certificates, and define
\[
 R_n^-=\left\{\max(0,\sqrt{B_n}-\eta_n)\right\}^2,
 \qquad
 R_n^+=(\sqrt{U_n}+\eta_n)^2.
\]
Then
\[
 R_n^-\leq\rho_n(c)\leq R_n^+.
\]
The projected rational-certificate procedure has worst-case risk at most \(R_n^+\), while the transferred rational prior certifies the lower bound \(R_n^-\).  If
\[
 \underline d_n=\frac{C_0(c)}n-R_n^+,
 \qquad
 \overline d_n=\frac{C_0(c)}n-R_n^-,
\]
then
\[
 \underline d_n\leq d_n(c)\leq\overline d_n
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0\leq\overline d_n-\underline d_n
 &=R_n^+-R_n^-\\
 &\leq\frac{5C_0(c^{(n)})}{4M_n^2}
 +4\sqrt{C_0(c^{(n)})}\,\eta_n n^{-1/2}
 +3\eta_n^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
One may choose the approximants so that \(\eta_n=o(n^{-5/6})\); with \(M_n=n\), the displayed improvement bracket then has width \(o(n^{-4/3})\).  If \(c\) is rational, one may take \(c^{(n)}=c\), and the direct exact-rational specialization with \(M_n=n\) has risk-certificate gap at most \(C_0(c)/(4n^2)\).

For \(c=c^\dagger\), one has \(C_0(c^\dagger)=1\), and the direct three-arm certificates satisfy, for every \(n,M\geq1\),
\[
 B_n(\nu_{n,M})\leq\rho_n(c^\dagger)\leq U_{n,M}
 \leq B_n(\nu_{n,M})+\frac1{4M^2}.
\]
The available exact rational calculations through \(n=5\) are the computed three-arm showcase for this formula; they are not used to infer a cross-\(n\) limit.

These conclusions establish exact analytic attainment for two active arms, explicit order attainment for every fixed number of active arms, and scale-matched computable procedure and converse certificates for every real zero-sum contrast, directly exact-rational when the contrast is rational.  They do not determine, when \(|S_c|\geq3\), convergence or the sharp constant of \(n^{4/3}d_n(c)\), sharp second-order optimality of \(q^\star\), convergence of the finite-program optimizers or priors, an analytic limiting feedback rule, or a limiting Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman, spectral, separable, or other operator.

First, if \(|S_c|=2\) and \(\rho_{n,2}=\rho_n((1,-1))\), then
\[
 \rho_n(c)=C_0(c)\rho_{n,2}.
\]
An exact finite-\(n\) saddle exists: take any minimax procedure and least-favorable complete-schedule prior supplied internally by the finite two-arm orbit game, map its two arms to the active sign pair, scale the estimator by \(\sqrt{C_0(c)}\), and push the prior forward by the sign-group schedule embedding. This existence statement does not specify the published scalar posterior mean or least-favorable prior. Moreover,
\[
 C_0(c)\kappa_c
 \leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)
 \leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)
 \leq43C_0(c),
\]
where \(\kappa_c>0\) is the explicit constant in the universal clipped-shrinkage theorem.

Second, for arbitrary support, the independent \(q^\star\) design and the explicit clipped-shrinkage estimator satisfy, for every sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \max_zR_n(\mathcal D^\star,\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sh}};z)
 \leq C_0(c)\{n^{-1}-\kappa_cn^{-4/3}\}.
\]

\[
 0<C_0(c)\kappa_c
 \leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)
 \leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)
 \leq43C_0(c).
\]

\[
 \eta_n=\frac{L_{c-c^{(n)}}}{2},
\]

\[

 \qquad U_n=U_{n,M_n}(c^{(n)}),
\]

\[

 \qquad R_n^+=(\sqrt{U_n}+\eta_n)^2.
\]

\[

\]

\[

\[
